name: veterinary_clinic_system_070_owner_lifetime_value_report
instruction: Produce the monthly owner financial report and the open-AR reconciliation for the practice, batched under the episode batch code in ops_reports. The owners.balance column is a stored cache and is NOT authoritative for open AR — many clients have a balance value that does not match what the invoice ledger says they owe; you must derive every financial number from billing_invoices and the patients roster, not from owners.balance. Create one ops_reports row with report='owner_ltv' for every owner in the system (all 220 owners, even if they have no pets or no invoices): {batch_code, owner_id, owner_name, lifetime_revenue, open_balance, invoice_count, pet_count, ar_current, ar_1_30, ar_31_60, ar_61_plus}. lifetime_revenue = sum of amount_paid over that owner's paid invoices. open_balance = sum of (total_amount - amount_paid) over sent or overdue invoices. invoice_count = count of all non-draft invoices for that owner (draft invoices are not billed yet and count toward nothing). pet_count = patients linked to that owner. The ar_* fields split open_balance into days-past-due buckets relative to the episode date (due_date vs episode date): ar_current for invoices not yet due or due on/after the episode date, ar_1_30 for 1-30 days past due, ar_31_60 for 31-60 days, ar_61_plus for 61+ days; the four buckets must sum to open_balance. Then create one report='owner_ltv_top' row {batch_code, owner_id, owner_name, lifetime_revenue} for the owner with the highest lifetime_revenue (tie broken by lowest owner_id). Finally create one report='owner_ar_reconciliation' row {batch_code, discrepancy_count, total_discrepancy} where discrepancy_count is the number of owners whose owners.balance does not equal the invoice-derived open_balance and total_discrepancy is the sum of absolute differences. No collection outside ops_reports may be modified.
_par_steps_note: measure via live gold run in QC session
_max_steps_note: measure via live gold run in QC session

success_criteria.summary: Recompute per-owner LTV, open AR, invoice count, pet count, and AR aging buckets from live invoices + patients (never owners.balance); exactly one owner_ltv row per owner, one owner_ltv_top row (highest LTV, tie -> lowest owner_id), and one owner_ar_reconciliation row (count + total absolute discrepancy between owners.balance and open_balance). All monetary values cents-exact; every derived aggregate verified by both a raw-row Python pass and an independent SQL pass which must agree with each other and with the written rows.

checks.expect: lifetime_revenue, open_balance, invoice_count and each ar_* bucket computed by a raw-row filter and by SQL aggregation must agree

hazards: owners.balance is a stale cache and disagrees with invoice-derived open AR for 58 owners; e.g. owner id=1 Margaret Whitfield has balance 134.00 but invoice id=1 (INV-1001, status 'sent', total 523.00, paid 0) leaves open AR 523.00; owner id=4 Carlos Mendoza has balance 175.00 but no open invoices; owner id=21 Eugene Kim has balance -45.00. Copying owners.balance into open_balance produces wrong values for most owners.
Invoice id=3 (INV-1003, owner_id 3, status 'draft', total 546.00) must not be counted in invoice_count, lifetime_revenue, open_balance, or any AR bucket — only non-draft invoices are billed.

Only two invoices are open in the seed: invoice id=1 (owner 1, sent, due_date 2026-08-21, 523.00 unpaid) and invoice id=2 (owner 2, sent, due_date 2026-09-20, 214.00 unpaid). The AR bucket each lands in depends on the episode date, which jitters +/-3 days per episode, so the bucket amounts are non-constant and must be derived live.
55 owners have zero pets (e.g. owner id=23 Jeffrey Robinson, who still has lifetime_revenue 1521.00). pet_count must be 0 for them, not dropped from the report.

The top owner is id=35 Carol Perez with lifetime_revenue 1970.00; the next owners are id=23 (1521.00), id=13 (1485.00), id=22 (1384.00). An agent that forgets the tie-break ordering or includes drafts computes the wrong top row.
